publications.description: One immutable generation of a program (a group's or a screen's): its exact manifest bytes, their SHA-256, a digest of its content and counts, its publisher and time.
publications.lifecycle: Inserted when a person publishes or restores; never edited. Superseded when the next generation of its program is published; pruned (manifest cleared, media references deleted) by maintenance once it is neither the latest, nor reported in use by a screen within seven days, nor within 90 days of being superseded (AT-18). Deleted only with its program. See docs/project/publication-sync-design.md.

id.description: Backend-generated immutable publication UUID, also in the manifest.

company_id.description: Company that owns the publication; immutable (tenant key).

program_id.description: Program this publication is a generation of; immutable.

branch_ids.description: Branches the program concerned when it was published (a group's explicit span or the screen's branch), so the media guard discloses only references the caller may see; empty for a whole-company group.
branch_ids.nullMeaning: Never null; an empty array means the program reached the whole company.

generation.description: Generation number within the program, from 1, increasing.

protocol.description: Synchronization protocol the manifest is serialized in.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical outputs, playlists and media, equal for equal content; republishing unchanged content returns the latest publication.

manifest.description: Exact UTF-8 JSON bytes served to screens, with schedules and media identifiers.
manifest.nullMeaning: The publication was pruned and can no longer be delivered or restored.

manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the manifest bytes, which authorization statements name.

media_bytes.description: Total size of the referenced display renditions.

restored_from_generation.description: Generation whose content this publication restored.

published_by_membership_id.description: Membership through which the publication was made.

superseded_at.description: PostgreSQL-clock instant the next generation was published.
superseded_at.nullMeaning: This is the program's latest publication.

pruned_at.description: PostgreSQL-clock instant maintenance pruned the publication.

objects.publications_generation_key: One publication per program and generation.
objects.publications_company_published_idx: Counts a company's recent publications for the publish limits.
objects.publications_company_id_fkey: A publication belongs to an existing company.
objects.publications_company_id_program_id_fkey: The program belongs to the same company; deleting a group's program deletes its publications.
objects.publications_published_by_principal_id_f: The publisher is a known principal.
objects.publications_company_id_published_by_mem: The publishing membership belongs to the same company.
objects.publications_branch_ids_present: The branch list is present and bounded.
objects.publications_manifest_until_pruned: The manifest is kept exactly until the publication is pruned.
objects.publications_manifest_size: The recorded size matches the stored manifest.
objects.publications_counts: Counts are not negative and stay within the snapshot limits.
objects.publications_restored_from: A restore names an earlier generation.
objects.publications_pruned_after_superseded: Only a superseded publication can be pruned.

publication_playlists.description: Each playlist copied into a publication, with the branch that owned it when it was published, so a restore can check the program's current reach.
publication_playlists.lifecycle: Inserted with its publication; never updated. Deleted with its publication.

company_id.description: Company that owns the publication; immutable (tenant key).

playlist_id.description: Copied playlist; not a foreign key, so the copy outlives the playlist.

branch_id.description: Branch that owned the playlist when it was published.
branch_id.nullMeaning: The playlist belonged to the whole company.

objects.publication_playlists_pkey: One row per playlist and publication.
objects.publication_playlists_company_id_publica: The publication belongs to the same company; rows go with it.
objects.publication_playlists_company_id_branch_: The owning branch belongs to the same company.

publication_media.description: Each media item of a retained publication with the display rendition delivered to screens; the publication media guard keeps these items from being deleted or purged.
publication_media.lifecycle: Inserted with its publication; never updated. Deleted when the publication is pruned or deleted.

company_id.description: Company that owns the publication; immutable (tenant key).

publication_id.description: Publication that references the media item.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the display rendition the manifest names.

content_type.description: Media type of the display rendition.

objects.publication_media_pkey: One row per media item and publication.
objects.publication_media_asset_idx: Finds the retained publications that protect a media item.
objects.publication_media_company_id_publication: The publication belongs to the same company; rows go with it.
objects.publication_media_company_id_media_asset: The media item belongs to the same company.
objects.publication_media_sha256: The rendition digest is a 32-byte SHA-256.

publication_device_states.description: The latest synchronization report of each screen as the screen stated it, with the time the server received it and the desired publication it answered. Reported publication IDs are untrusted.
publication_device_states.lifecycle: Inserted at a screen's first synchronization and overwritten by each later report. Kept with the device record.

company_id.description: Company that owns the screen; immutable (tenant key).

received_at.description: PostgreSQL-clock instant the last report was received; the panel's connection state derives from it (AT-24).

protocol.description: Protocol agreed for the last exchange.

desired_publication_id.description: Publication the server answered as desired.
desired_publication_id.nullMeaning: The screen's source had no publication.

active_publication_id.nullMeaning: The screen reported no active publication.

active_since.description: Activation time the screen reported, by its own clock.
active_since.nullMeaning: The screen reported no active publication.

recovery_publication_id.description: Previous valid publication the screen reported keeping.

staging_publication_id.nullMeaning: The screen reported no staging attempt.

staging_failure.description: Reported failure code of a failed staging attempt.

staging_bytes_done.description: Bytes the screen reported as downloaded for the attempt.

staging_bytes_total.description: Bytes the attempt needs, as the screen reported.

playback.description: Reported playback condition: PLAYING, NEUTRAL, AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, CLOCK_UNTRUSTED, DEGRADED or SETUP.

device_time.description: The screen's clock reading when it reported.

objects.publication_device_states_company_id_dev: The screen belongs to the same company.
objects.publication_device_states_staging: A staging attempt has a publication, a known state, a failure only when failed, and byte counts.
objects.publication_device_states_failure: Failure codes come from a closed set.
objects.publication_device_states_playback: Playback conditions come from a closed set.
objects.publication_device_states_storage: Storage is reported as a pair with free space within the total.

publication_device_events.description: Transitions in screens' synchronization reports: a newly desired publication delivered, an activation, a failed staging attempt or a playback change (AT-20).
publication_device_events.lifecycle: Inserted when a report changes; never updated. Deleted by maintenance 30 days after it occurred.

company_id.description: Company that owns the screen; immutable (tenant key).

occurred_at.description: PostgreSQL-clock instant the transition was received.

publication_id.description: Publication the transition concerns, as delivered or reported.
publication_id.nullMeaning: The transition concerns no publication, such as a playback change or an unpublished source.

objects.publication_device_events_device_idx: Reads a screen's recent transitions newest first.
objects.publication_device_events_company_id_dev: The screen belongs to the same company.
objects.publication_device_events_kind: Kinds come from a closed set.

publication_audit_events.description: Append-only record of publications and restores, with the acting member and the branches each program concerns.
publication_audit_events.lifecycle: Inserted in the same transaction as the publication it records; never updated or deleted at runtime. Retention follows the company (provisional until PH-13).

subject_id.description: Program the event concerns; not a foreign key, so events outlive deleted programs.

branch_ids.description: Branches the program concerns, for branch-scoped audit reads; empty for a whole-company group.
branch_ids.nullMeaning: Never null; an empty array means the program is company-wide.

actor_membership_id.description: Membership through which the publication was made.

details.description: Bounded summary: source kind, generation, counts and IDs; never manifest content.

objects.publication_audit_events_company_id_fkey: An event belongs to an existing company.
objects.publication_audit_events_actor_principal: The actor is a known principal.
objects.publication_audit_events_company_id_acto: The acting membership belongs to the same company.
objects.publication_audit_events_subject_idx: Reads a program's publication history newest first.
objects.publication_audit_events_branch_ids_pres: The branch list is present and bounded.
objects.publication_audit_events_subject_type: Subjects come from a closed set.
